narrative.intro: Regents of the University of California has $1.2B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date, from 3 awards with an average award size of $391M. Obligations fell 10.3% year over year. The Department of Energy is the primary buyer, providing $1.2B in obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences is the dominant market, receiving $1.2B of obligations. Historical obligations show large swings: FY21 obligations were $67.4M, FY22 obligations were $6.7M, FY23 obligations were $982M, FY24 obligations were $1.4B, and FY25 obligations were $1.3B. Smaller FY2026 buyers and markets include the Department of Commerce at $31.3K and Computer Facilities Management Services at $31.3K. Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools received $4M. Current-year totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date activity. The figures for largest awards and expiring contracts reflect total contract values where noted rather than year-to-date obligations. This profile is focused on the size and concentration of Regents of the University of California federal work in the current fiscal year.

sections.heading: How has Regents of the University of California's federal business trended over recent fiscal years?
sections.body: Regents of the University of California obligations rose and fell sharply across the last five years: FY21 obligations were $67.4M, FY22 obligations were $6.7M, FY23 obligations were $982M, FY24 obligations were $1.4B, and FY25 obligations were $1.3B. FY2026 to date obligations are $1.2B. Obligations fell 10.3% year over year.

sections.heading: Who are the main buyers and which markets drive Regents of the University of California's federal revenue?
sections.body: The Department of Energy is the main buyer, providing $1.2B in obligations in FY2026 to date. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences is the top market at $1.2B, with Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools at $4M and Computer Facilities Management Services at $31.3K. The Department of Commerce appears as a small buyer at $31.3K.

faq.q: How much does Regents of the University of California make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California has $1.2B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The university received 3 awards in the period with an average award size of $391M, and obligations fell 10.3% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Regents of the University of California?
faq.a: The Department of Energy buys most from Regents of the University of California, providing $1.2B in obligations in FY2026 to date. The Department of Commerce also appears as a buyer at $31.3K.

faq.q: What does Regents of the University of California sell to the government?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California sells research and development services and education-related services to the government, with Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences accounting for $1.2B. Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools account for $4M, and Computer Facilities Management Services account for $31.3K.

faq.q: Which Regents of the University of California contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: Current FY2026 to date data do not list specific expiring-contract line items in the summary figures. Largest markets and buyers include $1.2B in Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences and $1.2B from the Department of Energy, which indicates concentration but does not identify individual expiring contracts.
